workingTitle: Faint galaxies let JWST test dark matter in the early universe
topic: Cosmology & Early Universe / Gravity & Fundamental Physics
freshness: Unreviewed preprint submitted to arXiv on October 27, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: The analysis uses the ultraviolet luminosity function from JWST's GLIMPSE lensing program together with legacy Hubble and Subaru measurements at redshifts 4 to 8.
GLIMPSE uses magnification by galaxy cluster Abell S1063 to reach galaxies as faint as ultraviolet absolute magnitude about -12.
The inferred matter power spectrum agrees with cold dark matter within 0.2 dex at wavenumbers 3 to 9 per megaparsec and 0.5 dex at 9 to 27 per megaparsec.
For thermal-relic warm dark matter, the authors infer a particle-mass lower limit of 3.2 keV at 95 percent confidence.
The result probes sub-megaparsec structure around redshift 7, roughly 750 million years after the Big Bang.
caveats: The paper is an unreviewed preprint and its conclusions are preliminary.
Dark matter was not detected directly; the constraint is inferred by connecting galaxy counts to the abundance of dark matter halos.
The inference depends on models of early galaxy formation, high-redshift halo abundance, lensing, dust, and cosmic variance, although the authors test several variations.
The warm-dark-matter limit is weaker than some lower-redshift limits, but it uses a different epoch and different systematics.

sources.label: Muñoz et al., A GLIMPSE of Dark Matter: JWST Constraints on Early Structure Formation
